about: Finger Lakes Distilling sits on a hillside above the east shore of Seneca Lake, among the wineries of the Seneca Lake Wine Trail. Brian McKenzie founded it in 2007 with distiller Thomas Earl McKenzie; despite the shared name, the two are not related. It was one of the small group of craft distilleries that brought distilling back to New York, and it is now one of the oldest and largest in the state. About 95 percent of what it uses is grown locally, from corn and rye to wine grapes and fruit.

The gin shows what a distillery in wine country can do. Three-quarters of its neutral base is grape spirit that Finger Lakes Distilling distills itself on a column still. Sixteen botanicals, led by juniper with citrus, coriander and cucumber, are macerated in that spirit and redistilled in the distillery’s German-made pot still. It is bottled at 91 proof, in the London dry style, and is eligible under New York’s farm distillery license.

The McKenzie name also goes on the distillery’s whiskeys, its best-known line, made from grain grown by farmers a few miles from the stills and aged in its own rickhouses. In the gin, the juniper-forward London style meets the softer, slightly fruity texture of a grape base, with cucumber and citrus lifting the finish. It is a classic choice for a dry martini or a gin and tonic.
